title: Deprecation plan for legacy sync-embeddings endpoint and adaptive fallback aliases
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines the product requirements and acceptance criteria to deprecate the legacy synchronous embeddings endpoint (/v0/embeddings-sync) and the adaptive model-alias fallback behavior for the 'gpt-embed-legacy' family. The goal is to consolidate traffic on the unified /v1/embeddings API and eliminate an internal compatibility layer that increases maintenance burden and causes inconsistent performance profiles.
background: We currently support a legacy synchronous embeddings endpoint that many older SDKs and self-hosted clients still call. To avoid breaking customers, the platform provides an adaptive fallback that remaps legacy aliases (e.g., gpt-embed-legacy) to compatible model variants at request time. This compatibility layer increases latency variability, complicates batching, and prevents some runtime optimizations (KV reuse and prefix caching). Prior product work created /v1/embeddings with better batching, streaming/batch parity, and clearer model semantics. With increasing usage of /v1 and our limited engineering capacity to maintain the shim, we plan a staged deprecation of the legacy endpoint and alias fallbacks.
goals:
- Migrate >= 95% of actively used client keys off /v0/embeddings-sync to /v1/embeddings or SDK-adapter by the mandatory cutover date.
- Remove adaptive alias remapping so runtime can make deterministic routing and batching decisions.
- Provide migration tooling, SDK patches, and clear console warnings to minimize customer disruption.
- Ensure observability and telemetry gating to detect quality regressions early.
non_goals:
- Do not change model semantics or release new embedding model versions as part of this task.
- This ticket does not include migrations for unrelated legacy endpoints (e.g., legacy chatstream endpoints). Those are tracked separately.
timeline:
- 2026-02-20: Announcement blog + in-console banner + notice email to last 90-day callers.
- 2026-03-15: Opt-in migration mode enabled: requests to /v0/embeddings-sync are duplicated (server-side shadow) to /v1 and SDK adapters available. No customer-visible change.
- 2026-04-15: Mandatory cutover window begins: requests to /v0 receive a deprecation HTTP header and are rate-limited to encourage migration; increased telemetry and customer outreach.
- 2026-04-30: Final cutoff: /v0/embeddings-sync disabled for new requests; existing requests receive 410 for opt-in clients after repeated warnings.
- 2026-05-30: Remove alias remapping and related runtime compatibility code from production.
- 2026-06-30: Code deletion completed, documentation archived.
migration_steps: Publish SDK patch (JS/Python/Go) that transparently rewrites calls from /v0/embeddings-sync to /v1/embeddings and exposes a verbose migration warning logger.
Provide a lightweight CLI migration helper that scans client repositories for references to /v0/embeddings-sync or 'gpt-embed-legacy' aliases and produces recommended replacement snippets.
Enable server-side shadowing: mirror /v0 traffic to /v1 for a minimum of 30 days and collect token/latency/quality deltas to validate parity.
Create console usage reports showing remaining /v0 callers by org and contact engineering to offer migration assistance for high-usage customers.
Add an opt-in feature flag in the console for 'legacy-compat-mode' that customers can use to keep behavior for an additional 30 days post-cutoff if mutually agreed with support.
Publish a migration checklist for customers including example code, rate-limiting guidance, and fallback patterns for model alias changes.
acceptance_criteria: SDK releases (JS/Python/Go) published and downloadable with migration docs linked in SDK CHANGELOGs.
Shadowing telemetry pipeline shows token-level parity metrics and no unaddressed >5% quality regressions for top 50 customers within 14 days of shadowing.
Console exposes per-API-key migration status and a one-click opt-in to 'legacy-compat-mode' (for support-managed exceptions).
Operational runbook updated: on-call playbook for 410 spikes, rolling rollback steps, and customer communication templates are available.
Smoke tests cover both /v1 and the legacy path under shadowing and confirm batching/instrumentation metrics are captured.
Legal/compliance and security sign-off obtained because the migration touches model aliasing and audit logs (security_review_required = true).
telemetry_gates: Baseline: capture pre-shadow avg token latency, P95 latency, error rate, and vector similarity drift for a representative prompt set.
Gate 1 (Day 7): P95 latency under shadowing must be within +15% of baseline and error rate increase <0.5% for top 100 orgs.
Gate 2 (Day 21): Vector similarity (cosine) drift on canonical eval prompts <0.02 average; if exceeded, freeze cutover and triage.
Gate 3 (Pre-cutover): No unresolved high-severity incidents tied to alias remapping in last 14 days.
Telemetry ownership: runtime-observability + platform-qa to own dashboards and alerting rules.
rollout_plan: Phase A: Announce + documentation + SDKs. Monitor signups and surface 'at-risk' callers in console.
Phase B: Enable shadowing and collect parity metrics; proactively engage top-ten customers for manual migration assistance.
Phase C: Begin soft rate-limiting and deprecation headers; provide automated migration tickets for customers that accepted support help.
Phase D: Cutover and enforce 410 for non-exempt traffic; support-managed exemptions can be granted via 'legacy-compat-mode' for up to 30 days.
Phase E: Remove code paths and publish post-mortem/learnings.
rollback_criteria: If Gate 1 or Gate 2 telemetry thresholds are breached and triage cannot pinpoint fix within 48 hours, pause cutover and extend shadowing by 21 days.
If the error rate for customers in the top-10 revenue bucket increases by >1% after cutover, immediately re-enable compatibility aliasing for impacted tenant(s) and open a P0 engineering incident.
If a critical data integrity issue is found in mirrored responses, stop deprecation flow and issue an urgent rollback with customer notification.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Customer outages during cutover. Mitigation: multi-week shadowing, per-key notices, and temporary 'legacy-compat-mode' opt-outs.
Risk: Quality drift between legacy alias mapping and canonical model. Mitigation: run canonical evals during shadowing and stop cutover if similarity drift exceeds threshold.
Risk: Operational load on support and SRE. Mitigation: pre-provision migration support slots and a dedicated on-call rotation during cutover window.
